We will plant now, as you say rain comes. Plant xi wheat on nine of our cleared plots, so we have food stored against lean times. I assign nine adults to farming this spring. The rest will tend other needs: two to foraging, two to hunting, and the rest to guard and keep watch while we work.

If you would have us test another path this season, name one ingredient or skill to try and I will tell the village.

I know wind when it moves the roofs and whistles in the trees. It is breath of the world, a thing we feel and see by what it does—drives rain, scatters dust, bends the corn. It may be spirit, or it may be plain wind. I will not bow to every whisper, but I will listen when it has work for us.

What would you have us do, spirit? If you are wind, tell us which way to carry our effort this spring: plant, test a new tool, or seek a place to trade for better wind’s favor.

I answer plain: we send grain. A portion now, and let them know the path of friendship is opened. We may offer a small gift of grain, and ask for word of their need in return, or offer to trade for goods or knowledge later.

I would set aside a fair handful of grain, enough to ease their hunger but not so much as to weak our own store. Let the messenger go with 100 units of xi wheat as a start, with word: if they cannot take all at once, they may keep what they need and trade back what they cannot spare.
